title: Cape Verde · Sal
blurb: Practical things worth knowing before (and while) you visit Sal, Cape Verde: places, food, beaches, trips, language and the people.

questions.q: How many of Cape Verde's ten main islands are inhabited?
questions.fact: Santa Luzia is the only main island without permanent residents.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Praia is on the island of Santiago, not on Sal.

questions.q: What does the name 'Sal' mean in Portuguese?
questions.fact: Salt mining shaped the island's history long before tourism.

questions.q: In which year did Cape Verde become independent from Portugal?
questions.fact: Independence leader Amílcar Cabral did not live to see it; he was killed in 1973.

questions.q: What did the Portuguese find when they reached the islands in the 1400s?
questions.fact: People were brought to settle and work the islands, which is why Cape Verdean culture blends Portuguese and West African roots.

questions.q: What is the main tourist resort town on Sal?
questions.fact: Santa Maria sits at the southern tip, beside the long beach and the pier.

questions.q: Which town is Sal's administrative centre, close to the airport?
questions.fact: Most locals live in or near Espargos; the resorts are further south.

questions.q: What is the airport code for Sal's airport?
questions.fact: Look for SID on your boarding pass and luggage tags.

questions.q: Roughly how long is the island of Sal from north to south?
questions.fact: It is long and thin, so almost everywhere is a short drive from the sea.

questions.q: What is the highest point on Sal?
questions.fact: Monte Grande is only about 400 metres high. Sal is one of the flattest islands in Cape Verde.

questions.q: Where does most of Sal's drinking water come from?
questions.fact: Sal has no rivers and very little rain, so water is precious: don't waste it.

questions.q: Which landscape best describes most of Sal?
questions.fact: Sal is one of the driest places in Cape Verde, with sunshine nearly every day.

questions.q: When does Sal get what little rain it has?
questions.fact: Even then, showers are short and rare.

questions.q: What sometimes makes the sky hazy over Cape Verde?
questions.fact: The dusty haze is sometimes called 'bruma seca'.

questions.q: Which turtle species nests on Sal's beaches in summer?
questions.fact: Cape Verde is one of the world's most important loggerhead nesting sites. Never shine bright lights on nesting beaches at night.

questions.q: Which sharks do visitors usually see in the shallows at Shark Bay near Palmeira?
questions.fact: Follow your guide's rules and keep calm; most sharks there are young and shy.

questions.q: Which huge animals visit Cape Verde's waters in late winter and spring?
questions.fact: Trips from Sal and neighbouring Boa Vista sometimes get a glimpse of them.

questions.q: What do the steady north-east trade winds make Sal famous for?
questions.fact: Kite Beach near Ponta Preta is a favourite spot.

questions.q: What makes the crater at Pedra de Lume special?
a: A black-sand beach inside a volcano
A salt lake you can float in
questions.fact: Salt was mined from the crater; today you can bob in the very salty water.

questions.q: The 'Blue Eye' at Buracona looks its bluest when…
a: the tide is lowest at dawn
questions.fact: Daylight pours into the lava pool through a gap in the rock.

questions.q: What is the wooden pier in Santa Maria best known for today?
questions.fact: It's a lively spot early in the day and a popular place to watch the sunset.

questions.q: What is Cape Verde's national dish?
questions.fact: A slow-cooked stew of corn and beans with fish or meat. Leftovers are fried for breakfast.

questions.q: Which two things are the base of a traditional cachupa?
questions.fact: It cooks for hours, so locals often make it in big batches.

questions.q: Grogue, the local spirit, is made from what?
questions.fact: Mixed with honey or molasses it becomes 'ponche'. It is stronger than it tastes, so take it easy.

questions.q: Which Cape Verdean singer was known as the 'Barefoot Diva'?
questions.fact: She came from Mindelo on São Vicente and made morna famous worldwide.

questions.q: Which slow, soulful music style is Cape Verde best known for?
questions.fact: Morna songs are often about love, the sea and leaving home.

questions.q: What does the Cape Verdean word 'sodade' mean?
questions.fact: It is the same idea as the Portuguese 'saudade' and the title of Cesária Évora's best-known song.

questions.q: Which lively accordion-driven dance music is popular at Cape Verdean parties?
questions.fact: Funaná comes from the island of Santiago.

questions.q: Which island is considered Cape Verde's cultural capital, famous for its carnival?
questions.fact: Its main town, Mindelo, has a music scene that the whole country is proud of.

questions.q: Which Santiago town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.fact: It was the first European colonial town in the tropics.

questions.q: Cape Verdean Creole (Kriolu) is based mainly on which language?
questions.fact: Portuguese is the official language, but Kriolu is what people speak at home.

questions.q: The escudo is fixed in value to which currency?
questions.fact: It is about 110 escudos to the euro.

questions.q: Which island is famous for wine and coffee grown on volcanic soil?
questions.fact: The vines and coffee bushes grow inside the huge crater of Pico do Fogo.

questions.q: Which island is known for steep green valleys and some of the best hiking in Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Its mountains catch the clouds, so it is far greener than flat, dry Sal.

questions.q: What is the main town on the island of Fogo?
questions.fact: São Filipe has old colonial houses with wooden balconies.

questions.q: Which side of the road do vehicles drive on in Cape Verde?
questions.fact: Remember this when crossing the road, especially if you're used to driving on the left.

questions.q: Cape Verde's people are proud of 'morabeza'. What does it mean?
questions.fact: It is the spirit of welcome that visitors often mention.

questions.q: Why did Sal's airport become important in the early days of long-distance flying?
a: It was a refuelling stop mid-Atlantic
It was the only runway for jets
It was Europe's main mail sorting point
It was a Portuguese military base
questions.fact: The flat, dry island was ideal for a runway.

questions.q: Which community on Fogo was hit hardest by the volcanic eruption of 2014?
questions.fact: Lava destroyed villages inside the crater, and people have since rebuilt.

questions.q: In which months do loggerhead turtles mainly nest on Sal's beaches?
questions.fact: Hatchlings head for the sea at night, so avoid bright lights near nesting beaches.

questions.q: What is 'pastel com diabo dentro' ('pastry with the devil inside')?
a: A baked pastry filled with goat cheese
A fried pastry filled with sugar cane
A sweet pastry filled with chilli jam
A fried pastry filled with spicy fish
questions.fact: The 'devil' is the hot pepper in the tuna filling.

questions.q: Xerém is a traditional dish based on what?
questions.fact: Corn is the heart of Cape Verdean cooking, from xerém to cachupa.

questions.q: What is the 'ferrinho' used in funaná music?
a: A metal bar scraped for rhythm
A small drum made from a gourd
A bamboo flute for slow tunes
A small guitar with four strings
questions.fact: Funaná is played with an accordion and a scraped iron bar.

questions.q: Which upbeat dance music is the livelier cousin of morna?
questions.fact: Coladeira has a quicker, more danceable beat than the slow, sad morna.

questions.q: In 2019, which Cape Verdean music was added to UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage?
questions.fact: Morna is often described as the soul of Cape Verde.

questions.q: Which Santiago tradition has women singing and drumming on rolled-up cloth?
questions.fact: The rhythm is beaten on cloth held between the knees.

questions.q: In Kriolu, what does 'Kuma ki bu sta?' mean?
questions.fact: Kriolu has different forms on different islands, but many people understand this one.

questions.q: On other islands, what is an 'aluguer'?
a: A donkey you can hire for hill walks
A stall selling fresh fish on the beach
A small ferry between nearby islands
questions.fact: Locals use aluguers to travel between towns; ask your hotel before using one.

questions.q: How many stars are in the ring on Cape Verde's flag?
questions.fact: One for each of the ten main islands, even though Santa Luzia has no permanent residents.

questions.q: What do the stars on this flag stand for?
questions.fact: The ring sits on the blue band, which stands for the sea and the sky.

questions.q: You're visiting from the UK. What do you need for this kind of socket?
a: An adaptor; the voltage is the same
A transformer to step the power up
questions.fact: Cape Verde uses two round pin plugs (types C and F) at 230 V, so most chargers just need an adaptor.

questions.q: This clock shows 3pm in the UK on a summer day (British Summer Time). What time is it on Sal?
questions.fact: Cape Verde is UTC−1 all year with no clock changes, so it is 2 hours behind the UK in summer.

questions.q: This clock shows noon in the UK on a winter day (GMT). What time is it on Sal?
questions.fact: In UK winter, Cape Verde is just 1 hour behind.

questions.q: A beer in a beach bar costs 330 escudos (CVE). About how much is that in euros?
questions.fact: The escudo is pegged to the euro at roughly 110 CVE to €1, so divide by about 110.

questions.q: Lunch comes to 1,100 escudos. About how much is that in euros?
questions.fact: Roughly 110 CVE to €1.

questions.q: A dinner for two is 2,750 escudos. About how much is that in euros?
questions.fact: Roughly 110 CVE to €1.

questions.q: A red flag is flying on the beach. What does it mean?
a: The beach is for water sports only
Lifeguards are on duty, swim freely
questions.fact: Sal's open Atlantic beaches can have strong currents and waves, so take beach flags seriously.

questions.q: A yellow flag is flying on the beach. What does it usually mean?
a: The beach is closed for cleaning
questions.fact: Green means low hazard, yellow medium and red high hazard.

questions.q: What sport is shown here, which the steady winds make Sal famous for?
questions.fact: Sal has wind most of the year. Santa Maria has schools for beginners, and Ponta Preta is known for waves.

questions.q: You find a turtle laying eggs on the beach at night. What is the right thing to do?
a: Block her path to get a better photo
Watch quietly from a distance, no flash
Shine a torch so friends can see her
Help her dig the nest quickly
questions.fact: Light and noise can scare her back to sea before she lays. Loggerheads nest on Sal from about June to October.

questions.q: Tap the island called Sal, where you are heading.
questions.fact: Sal means 'salt'. It's small, flat and dry, in the east of the archipelago.

questions.q: Tap Boa Vista: the island with huge dunes and miles of empty beach, close to Sal.
questions.fact: Boa Vista means 'good view'. Its main town is Sal Rei.

questions.q: Tap the island with the capital city, Praia.
questions.fact: Santiago is the biggest island and has the most people. Cidade Velha is a UNESCO site here.

questions.q: Tap the island with the active volcano, Pico do Fogo.
questions.fact: Fogo means 'fire'. The volcano last erupted in 2014 and people still live in its crater.

questions.q: Tap the island of music and Cesária Évora, with the town of Mindelo.
questions.fact: Mindelo has the best-known nightlife and the carnival.

questions.q: Tap the green, mountainous island that you reach by ferry from Mindelo, famous for hiking.
questions.fact: The ferry from São Vicente takes about an hour.

questions.q: Tap Brava, the 'Island of Flowers', the smallest inhabited island.
questions.fact: You reach Brava by boat from Fogo.

questions.q: Tap the only main island with no permanent residents.
questions.fact: It's a nature reserve with seabirds and lizards found nowhere else.

questions.q: Tap Sal's nearest neighbour: the island just to its south.
questions.fact: It is about 55 km away. The two islands are the most visited in Cape Verde.

questions.q: Tap Maio, the quiet, flat island with long empty beaches, south of Boa Vista.
questions.fact: It's one of the least visited islands and has a lot of turtle nesting.

questions.q: Tap São Nicolau, the long island in the middle of the northern group.
questions.fact: It has mountains and a pointy skyline, with a lot of hiking and little tourism.

questions.q: Tap the resort town at the southern tip, with the long beach and the pier.
questions.fact: Most hotels, restaurants and the main beach are here, about 20 minutes from the airport.

questions.q: Tap Espargos, the main town next to the airport.
questions.fact: Most locals live here. It is the island's administrative centre.

questions.q: Tap Pedra de Lume, where a salt lake sits inside an old volcanic crater.
questions.fact: You can float in the salty water. Salt was mined here for centuries.

questions.q: Tap Buracona, home of the 'Blue Eye' pool, on the north-west coast.
questions.fact: The pool glows bluest when the sun is high overhead.

questions.q: Tap Palmeira, the small port on the west coast near Shark Bay.
questions.fact: Visitors see young lemon sharks in the shallows nearby.

questions.q: Roughly how far is Santa Maria from Sal's airport?
questions.fact: A transfer takes 20 to 30 minutes. Sal is only about 30 km long.

questions.q: Before flying to Cape Verde, what do most visitors have to complete online?
a: Pre-arrival registration and a security fee
questions.fact: Rules change, so always check the official government site before you travel.

questions.q: You hop in a taxi that has no meter. What should you do before setting off?
a: Ask for a receipt before you get out
Wait and pay whatever the driver asks
questions.fact: Taxi prices are often fixed for common routes, so ask your hotel what's fair.

questions.q: Can you pay in euros on Sal?
a: Often yes, but change comes in escudos
Only if you pay by credit card
Only at the airport exchange desk
questions.fact: It's still worth carrying some escudos for small shops, markets and taxis.

questions.q: What is the usual tip in a tourist-area restaurant with no service charge?
questions.fact: Staff are paid modestly, so tips are appreciated. Check the bill for an added service charge first.

questions.q: Where are you most likely to need cash?
questions.fact: Cards are usual in hotels and bigger restaurants, but smaller places often take cash only.

questions.q: At the craft stalls in Santa Maria, what's normal?
questions.fact: A smile and a fair counter-offer go a long way.

questions.q: What do most visitors do about drinking water?
a: Tap water straight from any tap
questions.fact: Sal's tap water is desalinated seawater. Bottled water is cheap and widely sold.

questions.q: In 2024 Cape Verde was certified free of which disease?
questions.fact: Mosquito bites are still best avoided, as dengue outbreaks have occurred.

questions.q: Which months are the hottest and most humid on Sal?
questions.fact: Air temperatures reach 30°C or more, and the sea is at its warmest too.

questions.q: How warm is the sea around Sal in February?
questions.fact: It's refreshing rather than cold. The sea reaches about 26 to 27°C in late summer.

questions.q: Away from the beach, in shops, restaurants and towns, what is polite to wear?
questions.fact: Locals dress modestly in town, so throw a shirt or wrap over your swimwear.

questions.q: What is 'cachupa refogada'?
a: A cold cachupa salad with lime
Leftover cachupa, fried, often with an egg
A sweet cachupa dessert with cream
questions.fact: A popular breakfast. Cachupa is cooked in big batches, so there is always some left.

questions.q: What is the difference between cachupa 'rica' and 'pobre'?
a: Rica is sweet; pobre is spicy
Rica is served cold; pobre hot
Rica uses rice; pobre uses potato
Rica has more meats; pobre is simpler
questions.fact: 'Rica' means rich and 'pobre' means poor.

questions.q: 'Ponche' is grogue mixed with what?
a: Honey or molasses, often with lime
questions.fact: It's sweeter than it tastes and stronger than it looks. Go gently.

questions.q: What is Cape Verdean 'cuscuz'?
a: A steamed maize cake for breakfast
A spicy fish soup with beans
questions.fact: It's usually served with butter, milk or sugar, or as a savoury side.

questions.q: Which of these is a Cape Verdean beer?
questions.fact: Sagres and Super Bock are Portuguese and also easy to find.

questions.q: What is 'lagosta' on a Cape Verdean menu?
questions.fact: A local speciality. It's often priced by weight, so ask the price per kilo before you order.

questions.q: What are 'lulas' on a menu?
questions.fact: Look for 'lulas grelhadas' (grilled squid) or 'polvo' (octopus).

questions.q: What is 'camarão' on a menu?
questions.fact: Frango is chicken, atum is tuna, carne is meat and queijo is cheese.

questions.q: What is a 'papo seco'?
questions.fact: You'll see them at breakfast and in bakeries.

questions.q: You ask for 'sem gelo' in your drink. What are you asking for?
questions.fact: Ice is usually fine in hotels, but some visitors prefer to skip it elsewhere.

questions.q: What do you get if you order 'água sem gás'?
questions.fact: 'Com gás' is sparkling.

questions.q: In Portuguese, what is 'pequeno-almoço'?
questions.fact: Almoço is lunch and jantar is dinner. Hotel signs often use these words.

questions.q: On your booking, what does 'meia pensão' mean?
a: Half board: breakfast plus one meal
A room with a shared bathroom
questions.fact: 'Pensão completa' is full board and 'tudo incluído' is all inclusive.

questions.q: What does a 'quarto duplo' mean on a booking?
questions.fact: 'Vista mar' means sea view.

questions.q: Why are most of Sal's big resorts around Santa Maria?
a: It's the old capital of the island
It's right next to the airport runway
The best long beach and calmer swimming
It's the only place with fresh water
questions.fact: The airport and Espargos are inland, but the beach is in the south.

questions.q: A resort advertises a 'Cape Verdean night'. What should you expect?
a: Live morna music and traditional dishes
A midnight swim in the lagoon
A quiz about the ten islands
questions.fact: It's a good chance to try cachupa and local dancing.

questions.q: About how many people live on Sal?
questions.fact: The population has grown quickly with tourism. Most people live in Espargos and Santa Maria.

questions.q: Compared with the number of people living on the islands, how many Cape Verdeans live abroad?
questions.fact: Big communities live in the USA, Portugal, France, the Netherlands and Italy.

questions.q: What is the national football team nicknamed?
questions.fact: 'Tubarões Azuis' in Portuguese. The team is a source of great pride.

questions.q: Which languages will you hear most in daily life on Sal?
questions.fact: Resort staff also speak English, Italian, German and French.

questions.q: In Portuguese a man says 'obrigado' for thank you. What does a woman say?
questions.fact: You match your own gender, not the listener's.

questions.q: When do you say 'Boa noite'?
a: In the evening or at night
questions.fact: 'Bom dia' is good morning and 'Boa tarde' is good afternoon.

questions.q: In Portuguese, what are you asking for with 'A conta, por favor'?
questions.fact: A useful phrase at the end of any meal.

questions.q: In Kriolu, what does 'sabi' mean?
questions.fact: You might say 'Es kumida sabi' ('this food is tasty').

questions.q: In Kriolu, what does 'Nha amigu' mean?
questions.fact: 'Nha' means 'my'. You'll hear it a lot.

questions.q: What does 'Boa Vista' mean in English?
questions.fact: Praia means beach, Sal means salt and Fogo means fire.

questions.q: What does 'Praia', the name of Cape Verde's capital, mean?
questions.fact: The city sits above a sheltered bay on Santiago.

questions.q: A typical island tour of Sal visits which places?
a: Pedra de Lume, Blue Eye, Shark Bay
Mindelo and the Monte Verde hike
Pico do Fogo and Cidade Velha
Viana Desert and Sal Rei town
questions.fact: Tours often last four to six hours. Take swimwear, sun cream and some cash.

questions.q: What is the 'mirage' at Terra Boa on Sal?
a: A floating island seen off the coast
A ghost story told on the road
An optical illusion of water on a plain
A hotel that seems to appear at night
questions.fact: It's caused by hot air over the flat salt plain.

questions.q: What happens when you bathe in the salt lake at Pedra de Lume?
a: The water burns like strong acid
questions.fact: The water is saltier than the sea. Rinse off afterwards.

questions.q: Which spot in the south-west of Sal is famous for waves, kite and windsurf events?
questions.fact: Beginners usually learn on calmer water near Santa Maria.

questions.q: If caught in a strong current while swimming, what is the best advice?
a: Swim parallel to the shore, then in
Stay still and call for help
questions.fact: Raise an arm and signal for help if you're tired.

questions.q: When is the wind steadiest for kitesurfing and windsurfing on Sal?
a: Never, the sea is always calm
Only in the month of August
questions.fact: The trade winds blow for much of the year. Check with a local school.
